Al-Hubab ibn al-Mundhir.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Hubab ibn al-Mundhir.question: That Prophet Muhammad was able to recognize _____'s idea as a preferable strategy is considered an admirable trait on behalf of the former

Al-Mu'addal.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mu'addal.question: The _____ was Saffarid ruler of Zarang in 911.
Al-Mu'addal.fact: Al-Mu'addal ibn Ali ibn al-Layth was the Saffarid ruler of Zarang for a part of 911. In 890 al-Mu'addal and his brother al-Layth helped their father 'Ali escape from imprisonment at the hands of the latter's uncle, the Saffarid amir Amr ibn al-Layth.

Al-Mu'addal.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mu'addal.question: The three of them fled to _____, where they entered the services of Rafi' ibn Harthama
Al-Mu'addal.fact: The three of them fled to Khurasan, where they entered the services of Rafi' ibn Harthama.

Al-Mu'addal.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mu'addal.question: After 'Ali died in 893, the brothers continued to serve _____'
Al-Mu'addal.fact: The three of them fled to Khurasan, where they entered the services of Rafi' ibn Harthama. After 'Ali died in 893, the brothers continued to serve Rafi'.

Al-Mu'addal.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mu'addal.question: Near the end of 908 al-Layth made a bid for power against 'Amr's son and successor Tahir by occupying part of _____
Al-Mu'addal.fact: Near the end of 908 al-Layth made a bid for power against 'Amr's son and successor Tahir by occupying part of Zarang.

Al-Mu'addal.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mu'addal.question: Al-_____ maintained his position, however, and Tahir was eventually forced to withdraw
Al-Mu'addal.fact: Near the end of 908 al-Layth made a bid for power against 'Amr's son and successor Tahir by occupying part of Zarang. Al-Mu'addal, who had been taken hostage by Tahir, was released in early 909 after Tahir was unable to dislodge al-Layth in an attempt to induce the latter to give up his struggle.

Al-Mu'addal.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mu'addal.question: Al-_____ was now amir, but many were opposed to him
Al-Mu'addal.fact: Near the end of 908 al-Layth made a bid for power against 'Amr's son and successor Tahir by occupying part of Zarang. Al-Mu'addal, who had been taken hostage by Tahir, was released in early 909 after Tahir was unable to dislodge al-Layth in an attempt to induce the latter to give up his struggle.

Al-Mu'addal.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mu'addal.question: He then moved on to _____ and killed a local leader there, but soon encountered stiff resistance and al-Layth was required to send him reinforcements
Al-Mu'addal.fact: He then moved on to Ghazna and killed a local leader there, but soon encountered stiff resistance and al-Layth was required to send him reinforcements.

Al-Mu'addal.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mu'addal.question: Despite this, he returned to _____ near the end of 909 having established the authority of al-Layth in the eastern provinces
Al-Mu'addal.fact: He then moved on to Ghazna and killed a local leader there, but soon encountered stiff resistance and al-Layth was required to send him reinforcements. Despite this, he returned to Sistan near the end of 909 having set up the authority of al-Layth in the eastern provinces.

Al-Mu'addal.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mu'addal.question: In Zarang, meanwhile, news of al-Layth's fall caused the people to recognize another brother, _____, as amir
Al-Mu'addal.fact: In Zarang, meanwhile, news of al-Layth's fall caused the people to recognize another brother, Muhammad, as amir. In an effort to cement his power, Muhammad imprisoned al-Mu'addal.

Al-Mu'addal.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mu'addal.question: Muhammad was subsequently forced to conduct a campaign against the _____ to the north
Al-Mu'addal.fact: Muhammad was subsequently forced to conduct a campaign against the Samanids to the north.

Al-Mu'addal.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mu'addal.question: Soon afterwards the _____ ibn Isma'il sent an army to take Zarang from the Saffarids
Al-Mu'addal.fact: Soon afterwards the Samanid Ahmad ibn Isma'il sent an army to take Zarang from the Saffarids.

Al-Mu'addal.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mu'addal.question: The Samanids arrived before the city in _____ 911 and initiated a siege
Al-Mu'addal.fact: The Samanids arrived before the city in March 911 and initiated a siege.

Al-Mu'addal.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mu'addal.question: This prompted him to negotiate with the _____, and at the end of July 911 he surrendered
Al-Mu'addal.fact: The Samanids arrived before the city in March 911 and initiated a siege. This prompted him to negotiate with the Samanids, and at the end of July 911 he surrendered.

Al-Mu'addal.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mu'addal.question: His surrender allowed the _____ to take control of Sistan
Al-Mu'addal.fact: This prompted him to negotiate with the Samanids, and at the end of July 911 he surrendered. His surrender allowed the Samanids to take control of Sistan.

Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.question: The _____ was Companion of Muhammad and Muslim commander.
Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.fact: Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya ibn al-Mughira ibn Abd Allah (Arabic: المهاجر بن أبي أمية المغيرة بن عبد الله, romanized: Al-Muhājir ibn Abī Umayya ibn al-Mughīra ibn ʿAbd Allāh) was a companion of the Islamic prophet Muhammad from the Banu Makhzum clan and a Muslim commander active in Yemen during the Ridda wars (632–633).

Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.question: Al-Muhajir's father was _____, a son of al-Mughira ibn Abd Allah, a prominent pre-Islamic leader of the Makhzum in Mecca
Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.fact: Al-Muhajir's father was Abu Umayya Suhayl, a son of al-Mughira ibn Abd Allah, a prominent pre-Islamic leader of the Makhzum in Mecca.

Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.question: Abu Umayya was well known for his generosity to traveling companions on the road and was popularly known as Zad al-Rakb (_____ for the Passengers)
Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.fact: Abu Umayya was well known for his generosity to traveling companions on the road and was popularly called Zad al-Rakb (Provider for the Passengers).

Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.question: Al-_____'s mother was Atika bint Amir from the Firas clan of the Kinana tribe, which was noted for its martial prowess
Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.fact: Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya ibn al-Mughira ibn Abd Allah (Arabic: المهاجر بن أبي أمية المغيرة بن عبد الله, romanized: Al-Muhājir ibn Abī Umayya ibn al-Mughīra ibn ʿAbd Allāh) was a companion of the Islamic prophet Muhammad from the Banu Makhzum clan and a Muslim commander active in Yemen during the Ridda wars (632–633). Al-Muhajir's father was Abu Umayya Suhayl, a son of al-Mughira ibn Abd Allah, a prominent pre-Islamic leader of the Makhzum in Mecca.

Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.question: Al-Muhajir's sister was _____, one of the wives of Muhammad
Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.fact: Al-Muhajir's sister was Umm Salama, one of the wives of Muhammad.

Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.question: He was a paternal first cousin of _____ ibn al-Walid
Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.fact: He was a paternal first cousin of Khalid ibn al-Walid.

Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.question: Muhammad appointed al-_____ as the tax collector over the Yemenite tribes of Kinda (specifically its Banu Mu'awiya branch) and Sadif
Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.fact: Al-Muhajir's mother was Atika bint Amir from the Firas clan of the Kinana tribe, which was noted for its martial prowess. Al-Muhajir's sister was Umm Salama, one of the wives of Muhammad.

Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.question: He married Asma bint al-Nu'man ibn Abi al-Jawn, a Kindite noblewoman and former wife of Muhammad; she later married al-Muhajir's Makhzumite kinsman Ikrima ibn _____
Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.fact: He married Asma bint al-Nu'man ibn Abi al-Jawn, a Kindite noblewoman and former wife of Muhammad; she later married al-Muhajir's Makhzumite kinsman Ikrima ibn Abi Jahl.

Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.question: In 631 _____ appointed al-Muhajir governor of Yemen's principal city Sana'a
Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.fact: Muhammad appointed al-Muhajir as the tax collector over the Yemenite tribes of Kinda (specifically its Banu Mu'awiya branch) and Sadif. He married Asma bint al-Nu'man ibn Abi al-Jawn, a Kindite noblewoman and former wife of Muhammad; she later married al-Muhajir's Makhzumite kinsman Ikrima ibn Abi Jahl.

Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.question: He did not take up the post, remaining in Medina until the accession of _____ in 632
Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.fact: He did not take up the post, remaining in Medina until the accession of Caliph Abu Bakr in 632.

Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.question: The Kinda was ultimately surrendered to al-_____ and Ikrima
Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.fact: In 631 Muhammad appointed al-Muhajir governor of Yemen's principal city Sana'a. Abu Bakr dispatched al-Muhajir to reinforce the governor of Yemen, Ziyad ibn Labid al-Ansari, and suppress the rebellion of the Banu Mu'awiya clan of Kinda in Hadhramawt (south Arabian coastal region) during the Ridda wars.

Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.question: The _____ was Ansar tribal chieftain and Muhammad's Companion.
Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.fact: Al-Mundhir ibn Amr al-Ansari (Arabic: المنذر بن عمرو) was a companion of Muhammad and a prominent chieftain of the Ansar from the Banu Sa'ida clan of the Khazraj tribe.

Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.question: He was one of the early converts to Islam in _____ and was among the seventy who pledged their loyalty at the Second pledge at al-Aqabah
Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.fact: He was one of the early converts to Islam in Medina and was among the seventy who pledged their loyalty at the Second pledge at al-Aqabah.

Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.question: Known by the epithet A'naq al-Mawt (أعنق ليموت, "The one who hastens to death") due to his extreme bravery, Al-_____ held significant command roles during the early Muslim military campaigns
Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.fact: Al-Mundhir ibn Amr al-Ansari (Arabic: المنذر بن عمرو) was a companion of Muhammad and a prominent chieftain of the Ansar from the Banu Sa'ida clan of the Khazraj tribe. Known by the epithet A'naq al-Mawt (أعنق ليموت, "The one who hastens to death") due to his extreme bravery, Al-Mundhir held significant command roles during the early Muslim military campaigns.

Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.question: At the _____ of Uhud in 625 CE, he was appointed by Muhammad as a commander of the infantry's left wing
Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.fact: At the Battle of Uhud in 625 CE, he was appointed by Muhammad as a commander of the infantry's left wing.

Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.question: His lineage is traced back through Lawdhan ibn '_____ to the progenitor of the Khazraj tribe
Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.fact: His lineage is traced back through Lawdhan ibn 'Abd Wudd to the progenitor of the Khazraj tribe.

Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.question: His mother was Hind bint al-_____ from the Banu Salama clan
Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.fact: Known by the epithet A'naq al-Mawt (أعنق ليموت, "The one who hastens to death") due to his extreme bravery, Al-Mundhir held significant command roles during the early Muslim military campaigns. His mother was Hind bint al-Mundhir from the Banu Salama clan.

Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.question: Notably, Al-_____ was literate and capable of writing in Arabic prior to the advent of Islam, a skill that was relatively rare in Arabia at the time

Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.question: Following his conversion, he partnered with Sa'd ibn 'Ubada and _____ to destroy the idols belonging to the Banu Sa'ida clan
Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.fact: Following his conversion, he partnered with Sa'd ibn 'Ubada and Abu Dujana to destroy the idols belonging to the Banu Sa'ida clan.

Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.question: He was later selected as one of the twelve _____ (tribal representatives) during the Second pledge at al-Aqabah, where he pledged his life and loyalty to Muhammad
Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.fact: He was later selected as one of the twelve Nuqaba (tribal representatives) during the Second pledge at al-Aqabah, where he pledged his life and loyalty to Muhammad.

Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.question: During the _____ of Uhud the following year, he was entrusted by Muhammad with the command of the infantry's left wing, demonstrating his high standing within the early Muslim military hierarchy
Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.fact: During the Battle of Uhud the following year, he was entrusted by Muhammad with the command of the infantry's left wing, demonstrating his high standing within the early Muslim military hierarchy.

Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.question: The mission was initiated following a request from the chieftain _____, who had provided a guarantee of safety (amān) for the Muslim emissaries
Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.fact: The mission was initiated following a request from the chieftain Abu Bara, who had provided a guarantee of safety (amān) for the Muslim emissaries.

Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.question: However, upon reaching the well of Bi'r Ma'una, the party was betrayed and surrounded by the tribes of _____, led by Amir ibn al-Tufayl
Al-Mundhir ibn Amr.fact: However, upon reaching the well of Bi'r Ma'una, the party was betrayed and surrounded by the tribes of Banu Sulaym, led by Amir ibn al-Tufayl.
